headline: Bond vol went vertical — MOVE +55% in a month at z=3.07 — while VIX sits at 15.3 in the 10th percentile, and the only thing that cracked the dollar was a Brazilian election.
summary: The rates composite deteriorated again, from -78 to -85, the worst reading on the board. The 10-year is +3bp to 5.31% at the 100th percentile of 52 weeks (+53bp on the month), the 30-year 5.66%, the 5-year 5.06% at the 98th, and the 10-year real yield printed another new high at 2.95% with z=2.05 and acceleration 1.47. None of this is inflation: 10y breakevens are 2.36%, up 1bp on the month, and 5y breakevens are rolling over with acceleration -0.64. This is pure real rate and term premium, and the front end is tightening with it — the 3m bill +31bp on the month to 4.22%. What is genuinely new today is the volatility: MOVE is +5.9% on the day, +11.6% on the week and +55.4% on the month to 113.6, z=3.07 with acceleration 1.99 — the single most extreme series in the entire digest. That is accelerating in the wrong direction. TLT is at the 0th percentile of the year, IEF at the 0th, LQD at the 1st, and the 30-year mortgage at 7.28% sits at the 100th.

Equity vol is still priced as if the bond market is a rumour. VIX 15.32 (10th percentile), VIX3M 18.0 (5th percentile), term structure 0.862, and SKEW decaying with acceleration -1.79 — against bond vol in the 98th. The index itself is fine: SPX +0.7% to 7774 at the 98th percentile, NDX +0.9%, QQQ/SPY z=1.69. The composition is not. RSP/SPY is at the 3.7th percentile of 52 weeks with z=-1.88, IWM/SPY -4.8% on the month, DJT -5.8%, DJI -4.0%, equal-weight -3.2%. All the index gain is in a narrowing cohort: SOXX +13.5% on the month, SMH +11.8%, CIBR +12.1% (z=1.50, acceleration 1.54), AMD +32.3%, META +20.4%, TSM +13.6%. Breadth composite -8, risk regime -8. You are being paid nothing to own convexity against a tape where the average stock has been losing to the index for a month.

The dollar finally gave ground, and the reason is idiosyncratic, not macro. DXY -0.4% to 101.79 (still z=1.32 and turning up, 94th percentile), EURUSD +0.2% to 1.1279 but still at the 4th percentile. The actual move was Brazil: USDBRL -4.4% in a single session, Bovespa +7.7% to a record 206,910 (+13.1% on the week, z=2.01), EWZ +12.5% on the day and +18.7% on the week at the 100th percentile — the first-round election result with a runoff on 25 October. That dragged the whole complex: ARGT +5.9%, USDMXN -1.2% (though still z=2.33 with acceleration 1.98 and +6.1% on the month), CEW +0.6%, EEM +1.6%, KWEB +2.9%, FXI +2.0%, EEM/SPY turning up. Europe is the mirror image — EFA/SPY at the 0th percentile, EWG -6.0% on the month, EWI -7.1%, EWP -6.7%. This is not dollar weakness; it is one country re-rating.

Commodities turned and equities haven't marked it. WTI -2.1% to 87.52 with acceleration -1.67, Brent -2.2% to 98.13 (-4.3% on the week, down from 102.70 three sessions ago), RBOB -6.5% on the day and -7.4% on the week. Yet OIH +3.1%, XOP +1.4%, XLE +1.0%. Copper is the one honest cyclical, +1.0% to 6.65 with copper/gold at the 97th percentile (z=1.07, acceleration 1.30) and XLI/XLU +4.1% on the month with acceleration 1.34 — growth pulse +18. Gold bounced +1.1% to 4201 after a -6.2% month, but miners refuse to confirm: GDX z=-1.35 with acceleration -2.10, GDX/gold acceleration -2.09, NEM acceleration -2.12. Credit remains the hinge that is holding — HYG/IEF +0.2% at the 97th percentile, BKLN at the 93rd, credit composite 40 — so HYG's -2.3% month is duration, not default. The carnage is concentrated in the discount-rate victims: the power/nuclear complex is capitulating (NLR -13.5% on the month at the 1.7th percentile, REMX -16.0% at the 2.4th, URA -12.7%, CEG -10.5%), financials are in open liquidation (GS z=-2.01, BX -18.0% on the month, IAI -9.3%, XLF -6.9%), and housing is at zero (ITB -8.1% at the 0.8th percentile, HD -12.4% at the 0th, XHB/SPY at the 0th).

good.text: Credit has not blinked. HYG/IEF +0.2% to the 97th percentile, BKLN unchanged at the 93rd, HYG +0.1% — spreads are intact even as IG duration bleeds (LQD -3.0% on the month, 1st percentile). Credit composite 40 is the strongest reading on the board.

The dollar cracked for the first time in a week and EM took the bid: USDBRL -4.4% on the day, EWZ +12.5%, Bovespa +7.7% to a record (z=2.01), ARGT +5.9%, USDMXN -1.2%, CEW +0.6%, EEM +1.6% with EEM/SPY turning up.

AI leadership is widening, not narrowing to one name. SOXX +13.5% and SMH +11.8% on the month, TSM +2.8% on the day at the 100th percentile, AMD +32.3% on the month, CIBR +12.1% with z=1.50 and acceleration 1.54, IGV turning up +4.9%.

The speculative tail is reviving off a low base: ARKK +3.3% on the day at the 100th percentile, IPO +2.1%, BTC +7.4% on the month turning up, SOL +13.1%, MSTR +15.1% on the month and +63.2% on three — all still in the bottom half of their 52-week ranges.

The growth pulse held through the rates shock. Copper +1.0% at the 92nd percentile, copper/gold at the 97th with acceleration 1.30, XLI/XLU +4.1% on the month (acceleration 1.34), Nikkei +7.9% on the week, TWII at the 100th percentile.

Energy inflation is deflating fast: RBOB -6.5% on the day and -5.6% on the month, WTI -4.3% on the month with acceleration -1.67, and 5y breakevens rolling over at 2.36% with acceleration -0.64. The bond selloff is not a CPI problem.

bad.text: Real yields made another new high — 10y TIPS 2.95%, z=2.05, acceleration 1.47, 38% above its 200-day. With 10y breakevens at 2.36% and flat, every basis point of the 10y at 5.31% (100th percentile) and 30y at 5.66% is term premium. Rates composite -85, worse than yesterday's -78.

MOVE is the most extreme series on the board: 113.6, +5.9% on the day, +55.4% on the month, z=3.07, acceleration 1.99. That is an accelerating tightening, not a bullish acceleration. TLT, IEF and LQD are all at the 0th-1st percentile of 52 weeks.

Breadth kept deteriorating even as SPX rose 0.7%. RSP/SPY flat on the day but z=-1.88 at the 3.7th percentile of the year, IWM/SPY -4.8% on the month, DJT -5.8%, DJI -4.0%, SPW -3.2%. Yesterday's one-day breadth repair did not follow through.

Financials are being liquidated despite the steepest 3m10y of the year at +1.09. GS z=-2.01 and -14.0% on the month, BX -18.0% (z=-1.86), IAI -9.3% with acceleration -1.40, XLF -6.9%, KBE -7.0%, KRE/SPY -6.7%.

The rate-sensitive consumer is at zero with no shelter. 30y mortgage 7.28% at the 100th percentile (+62bp on the month, acceleration 1.27), ITB -8.1% at the 0.8th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 0th, HD -12.4% at the 0th, DHI -1.3%, NKE at the 0.3rd, MCD at the 2nd.

The power/electrification trade is in capitulation: NLR -13.5% on the month at the 1.7th percentile (z=-1.96), REMX -16.0% at the 2.4th, URA -12.7%, TAN -9.1% at the 2nd, CEG -10.5% and VST -2.8% despite today's bounce. Gold miners are also failing to confirm gold's +1.1% — GDX acceleration -2.10.

trades.name: Equity vol against bond vol
trades.line: Long VIX/SPX convexity vs MOVE at z=3.07
trades.expr: Buy VIX Nov 20/30 call spreads, or SPY Dec 3-month 5%-OTM put spreads financed by selling 1-month 3%-OTM puts. Size for carry bleed of ~2 vol points.
trades.thesis: Bond vol at a 3-sigma monthly expansion has never coexisted for long with equity vol in the 10th percentile. Either MOVE mean-reverts (unlikely with real yields making new highs daily) or VIX catches up. The convexity is being given away.
trades.trigger: MOVE 113.6, +55.4% on the month, z=3.07, acceleration 1.99 — the most extreme print in the digest — against VIX 15.32 at the 10th percentile, VIX3M 18.0 at the 5th, term structure 0.862, and SKEW decaying with acceleration -1.79.
trades.stop: MOVE back under 95 with the 10y below 5.10% and VIX3M holding 17 — that is the benign resolution and the structure is dead money.
trades.target: VIX 22-25 on any 3% SPX drawdown; 2.5-3x on the call spread.

trades.name: Long-end Treasuries
trades.line: Short TLT: 30y 5.66%, term premium still widening
trades.expr: Buy TLT Dec 76 puts or short TLT outright against a long in 2-year notes (duration-neutral steepener). Alternative: short the 30y future (ZB).
trades.thesis: The selloff is term premium, not inflation — 10y breakevens are 2.36% and flat while the 10y real yield makes new highs. That is the kind of move that does not stop at round numbers, and bond vol accelerating confirms there is no stable marginal buyer at these levels.
trades.trigger: 30y 5.66% (+42bp on the month), 10y 5.31% at the 100th percentile, DFII10 2.95% with z=2.05 and acceleration 1.47, TLT -5.8% on the month at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks. 2s10s +15bp on the week to 0.47.
trades.stop: TLT closes above 81 (10y through 5.05%) or MOVE rolls back under 95 with a soft payroll print.

trades.name: Home construction
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.28% mortgage, 0.8th pctile, no bid
trades.expr: Short ITB outright or buy Jan 80 puts; pair against long SPY for a market-neutral version of the same discount-rate trade.
trades.thesis: Mortgage rates are at the highs of the cycle and still accelerating, and the group has already broken to the bottom of its 52-week range — this is not a washed-out contrarian long, it is a trend with a fresh fundamental catalyst every week the 10y makes a new high.
trades.trigger: 30y mortgage 7.28%, +62bp on the month, z=1.85 with acceleration 1.27 at the 100th percentile. ITB -1.2% on the day, -8.1% on the month, 0.8th percentile; XHB/SPY at the 0th percentile; HD -12.4% on the month at the 0th; DHI -6.7%.
trades.stop: 30y mortgage below 6.90% or ITB reclaims 93 (its 1-month highs) on expanding breadth in XHB.

trades.name: Brazil into the 25 October runoff
trades.line: Long EWZ call spread into the Oct 25 runoff
trades.expr: Buy EWZ Dec 44/52 call spreads rather than stock — the runoff on 25 October is binary and implied vol is cheaper than the realised 12.5% one-day move. Hedge FX exposure is already embedded.
trades.thesis: Brazil is re-rating on politics with the currency and the index moving together — the cleanest combination in EM. A call spread owns the second leg of the re-rating while capping the loss if the runoff reverses the first round.
trades.trigger: Bovespa +7.7% on the day to a record 206,910, +13.1% on the week, z=2.01; EWZ +12.5% on the day and +18.7% on the week at the 100th percentile; USDBRL -4.4% in one session to 4.9945, -8.8% YTD. Broad EM confirms: CEW +0.6%, EEM +1.6%, EEM/SPY turning up.
trades.stop: USDBRL back above 5.25 (reversing the entire election move) or EWZ closing below 38.

trades.name: Semis over brokers
trades.line: Long SMH / short IAI: AI vs financial liquidation
trades.expr: Long SMH, short an equal dollar amount of IAI. Rebalance monthly. Express the short via IAI rather than XLF to avoid the regional-bank squeeze risk.
trades.thesis: The tape is splitting along the discount rate: cash-generative AI capex compounders versus balance-sheet and fee businesses that need lower vol and tighter spreads. Bond vol at z=3.07 keeps capital markets shut; semis don't care.
trades.trigger: SMH +11.8% on the month, SOXX +13.5%, SMH/SPY z=1.43, TSM +2.8% on the day at the 100th percentile, AMD +32.3% on the month. Against IAI -9.3% on the month with z=-1.79 and acceleration -1.40, GS z=-2.01 and -14.0%, BX -18.0% (z=-1.86).
trades.stop: Pair drawdown of 7%, or SMH/SPY breaking back below its 1-month lows while IAI reclaims its 200-day (it sits 1.1% below).

trades.name: Energy equity catch-down
trades.line: Short XOP: Brent -4.3% wk, equities haven't marked it
trades.expr: Short XOP or buy Nov 180 puts; for a lower-beta version, short OIH into today's +3.1% bounce. Keep a long XOM tail if you want sector-neutrality.
trades.thesis: Crude is rolling over from an extremely extended base and the equities are still priced off the high. The commodity's acceleration has turned decisively negative while the stocks rallied on the day — that gap closes downward.
trades.trigger: WTI -2.1% to 87.52 with acceleration -1.67, Brent -2.2% to 98.13 and -4.3% on the week, RBOB -6.5% on the day and -7.4% on the week with acceleration -1.18, DBC acceleration -1.43. Yet XOP +1.4% and OIH +3.1% on the session, XOP still +22.2% on three months, XLE 3-month relative strength +16.2%.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 103 (last week's level) or WTI closes above 92 on a supply event.

trades.name: Crypto beta off a low base
trades.line: Long IBIT with MSTR as the high-beta sleeve
trades.expr: Core long IBIT, 1/3 sleeve in MSTR. Keep the MSTR sleeve small — it is -53.2% over 12 months and will halve on a liquidity shock.
trades.thesis: Crypto has quietly turned up across the board while still sitting in the bottom half of its 52-week range — the rare asset where the trend is improving but positioning is not crowded. It is also the cleanest expression of the dollar finally losing momentum.
trades.trigger: BTC +7.4% on the month and +36.3% on three, trend turning up, but only at the 42nd percentile of 52 weeks. ETH +7.9% on the month, SOL +13.1%, MSTR +15.1% on the month and +63.2% on three with relative strength turning up. ARKK +3.3% on the day at the 100th percentile confirms the speculative bid.
trades.stop: BTC closes below 78,000 (giving back the month) or DXY reasserts above 103 with the EM bid failing (CEW back below 19.20).
